record.original_question: Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group a variety?

evidence.quote: [J´ ons1953, sec. 5] Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group a variety?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{N}$ denote the class of all lattices $L$ such that there exists a group $G$ for which $L$ is isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice $\mathrm{Norm}(G)$ of normal subgroups of $G$ (ordered by inclusion, with meet given by intersection and join by the subgroup generated by the union, equivalently the product of normal subgroups).

Recall that a class $\mathcal{V}$ of lattices is called a variety if it is closed under the formation of homomorphic images, sublattices, and arbitrary direct products; equivalently, by Birkhoff's theorem, if it is the class of all lattices satisfying some set of lattice identities.

Question: Is $\mathcal{N}$ a variety of lattices?
artifact.category_tag: Lattice varieties and normal subgroup lattices
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turn up the survey "Varieties of groups and normal-subgroup lattices" (Algebra Universalis, 1994) discussing Jónsson-type problems on characterizing varieties via normal-subgroup lattices, but no clear resolution of the specific question of whether the class of lattices embeddable in some normal-subgroup lattice forms a lattice variety was located. The problem appears to remain open or at least is still cited as an open problem; status is recorded as unknown pending stronger evidence.

status_evidence.title: Varieties of groups and normal-subgroup lattices—a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on Jónsson's problem of characterising a variety of groups by means of the normal-subgroup lattices of its member groups.
status_evidence.claim: The question is part of an active line of research stemming from Jónsson 1953; no resolution found.

status_evidence.title: Lattice of subgroups - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Normal subgroups always form a modular lattice; every finite distributive lattice is isomorphic to the normal subgroup lattice of some group.
status_evidence.claim: Background facts about normal subgroup lattices, but no statement that the embeddability class is or is not a variety.
